optionD: The firm's inventory of the bond that day
explanation: Rule 2232(c) requires confirmations of these trades to show the execution time expressed to the second, with a reference and, for electronic confirmations, a link to FINRA's TRACE data page for the security.

question: A buying firm intends to buy in securities a seller has failed to deliver. Under Rule 11810 its written buy-in notice must reach the seller by:
optionA: 4 p.m. Eastern on the day of the buy-in
optionB: 12 noon Eastern, five business days before the buy-in
optionC: 12 noon Eastern, two business days before the buy-in
optionD: The close of business on the settlement date
explanation: Rule 11810(b)(1) requires written notice to be delivered to the seller's office not later than 12:00 noon Eastern time, two business days before execution of the proposed buy-in.

question: A firm receives a retransmitted buy-in notice from a party it owes securities to. It must pass the notice on so it reaches its own seller by:
optionA: The same time that is stated in the original notice
optionB: The end of the buy-in day
optionC: Three business days before the buy-in
optionD: 12 noon Eastern, the business day before the buy-in
explanation: Rule 11810(b)(5) requires immediate retransmittal, with the retransmitted notice delivered by 12 noon Eastern on the business day preceding the date of the proposed buy-in.

question: A customer sells stock in a cash account but has not delivered the shares 10 business days after the settlement date. Under SEC Rule 15c3-3(m) the firm must:
optionA: Close out the sale by buying in the shares
optionB: Extend the settlement date by 30 days
optionC: Cancel the sale and rebill the buyer
optionD: Report the customer to FINRA as a fail
explanation: Rule 15c3-3(m) requires a broker-dealer to close out a customer sell order by purchasing securities of like kind and quantity if the customer has not delivered them within 10 business days after the settlement date, unless an extension applies.

question: In an off-exchange trade between two FINRA member firms in an equity security, the trade report is generally made by:
optionA: The member on the buy side
optionB: The member on the sell side
optionC: Both members, as separate reports
optionD: The clearing firm of the buyer
explanation: Under FINRA's equity trade reporting rules, in a trade between two members the executing party is the sell-side member, which reports the trade; in a trade with a non-member or customer, the member reports.

question: Under FINRA Rule 6730, most corporate bond trades must be reported to TRACE as soon as practicable and no later than:
optionA: 15 minutes after execution
optionB: 10 seconds after execution
optionC: 1 hour after execution
optionD: The end of the trading day
explanation: Rule 6730(a)(1) sets an outer limit of 15 minutes for TRACE-eligible securities such as corporate bonds. FINRA withdrew its proposal to cut that window to one minute in Regulatory Notice 25-17.

question: Which trade is reported to FINRA's TRACE system?
optionA: A trade in a municipal bond
optionB: An exchange trade in a listed option
optionC: An exchange trade in a listed stock
optionD: A corporate bond trade
explanation: TRACE collects transactions in TRACE-eligible securities such as corporate, agency and Treasury debt. Municipal trades go to the MSRB, and exchange trades are reported by the exchanges.

question: A member executes a trade in an OTC equity security that is not an NMS stock. It reports the trade to:
optionA: The OTC Reporting Facility
optionB: A FINRA Trade Reporting Facility
optionC: The TRACE system for debt
optionD: The MSRB's RTRS system
explanation: Under the Rule 6600 Series, trades in OTC equity securities (non-NMS stocks) are reported to the ORF. Off-exchange trades in NMS stocks go to a Trade Reporting Facility or the Alternative Display Facility.

question: A retail customer buys a callable bond in a trade effected on the basis of yield to call. Besides that yield, the Rule 10b-10 confirmation must show:
optionA: The issuer's full credit rating history
optionB: The names of the other buyers in the issue
optionC: The type of call, the call date and the call price
optionD: The bond's credit rating at issue
explanation: Rule 10b-10(a)(6) requires, for a debt trade effected on the basis of yield, the yield used and its type, and if effected at yield to call, the type of call, the call date and the call price, plus the dollar price.

question: Under Rule 2231, a firm must send customers account statements at least:
optionA: Once each calendar quarter
optionB: Once each calendar year
optionC: Once every six months
optionD: Only in months with trades
explanation: Rule 2231 requires general securities members to send account statements at least once each calendar quarter to each customer with a balance or position, showing activity and positions.

question: An adviser places one block order for several of its managed accounts. To avoid favoring some accounts, the allocation should:
optionA: Be decided after seeing which accounts would profit
optionB: Give the best fills to the largest accounts
optionC: Be left to the trader's judgment each day
optionD: Follow a fair method set before or when it is placed
explanation: Allocating block trades after the results are known can let a firm favor some accounts. Supervisors should require a fair allocation method determined before or at the time of the order and documented.

question: A cash account customer buys stock and fails to pay by the Regulation T deadline, and the firm sells the stock out. Unless the firm gets relief, the account is:
optionA: Closed permanently by the firm
optionB: Frozen for 90 days: cash must be in before any purchase
optionC: Converted to a margin account with a call
optionD: Restricted only for the next trade the customer makes
explanation: Under Regulation T section 220.8, if a customer sells a security before paying for it or fails to pay, the account is frozen for 90 days, during which the customer must have cash in the account before any purchase is executed.

question: Under SEC Rule 15c6-2, for institutional trades that need allocations, confirmations and affirmations, a broker-dealer must have agreements or policies to complete them:
optionA: Within three business days after the trade date
optionB: By the end of the settlement date
optionC: As soon as practicable, by the end of trade date
optionD: Before the customer's next quarterly statement
explanation: Rule 15c6-2, adopted with the move to T+1 settlement, requires either written agreements or policies reasonably designed to ensure completion of allocations, confirmations and affirmations as soon as technologically practicable and no later than the end of trade date.

question: Under Section 5 of the Securities Act, before a registration statement is filed, an underwriter generally may not:
optionA: Make offers to sell the security
optionB: Hold internal syndicate planning talks
optionC: Publish routine research on other issuers
optionD: Perform due diligence on the issuer
explanation: Section 5(c) prohibits offers to sell or buy before a registration statement is filed, subject to safe harbors; Section 5(a) prohibits sales until it is effective. Preliminary negotiations among underwriters and the issuer are allowed.

question: During the waiting period, a firm may publish a notice limited to basic facts such as the issuer's name, the security, the price range and the underwriters under:
optionA: Rule 144
optionB: Rule 10b-5
optionC: Rule 134
optionD: Rule 15c3-1
explanation: Rule 134 permits limited communications, often called tombstone ads, that are not deemed a prospectus, once a registration statement has been filed.

question: A free writing prospectus used in a registered offering after the registration statement is filed must generally:
optionA: Carry a legend saying where to get the prospectus
optionB: Be reviewed and approved by the SEC before use
optionC: Be shorter than one printed page
optionD: Omit any information about price
explanation: Rule 433 requires a free writing prospectus to bear a prescribed legend stating that a registration statement and prospectus are filed and how to obtain them, and in many cases to be filed with the SEC.

question: SEC Rule 163B lets any issuer, or a person acting for it, test the waters before or after filing a registration statement with:
optionA: Retail investors who sign a written waiver
optionB: QIBs and institutional accredited investors
optionC: Any person who reads the issuer's website
optionD: Only the issuer's current employees
explanation: Rule 163B, adopted in 2019, extends test-the-waters communications to all issuers, but only with potential investors reasonably believed to be QIBs or institutional accredited investors.

question: Under FINRA Rule 5110, the underwriting terms of a public offering that must be filed with FINRA are due no later than:
optionA: The day the offering is priced
optionB: 30 days after the offering closes
optionC: Three business days after the SEC filing
optionD: Ten business days before the registration becomes effective
explanation: Rule 5110 requires the documents and information for a filed public offering to be submitted to FINRA no later than three business days after filing with the SEC, and FINRA must state it has no objection before the offering proceeds.

question: Unregistered securities that an underwriter receives as compensation in an IPO are generally subject under Rule 5110 to a lock-up of:
optionA: 30 days from the effective date
optionB: 90 days from the pricing date
optionC: One year from the offering's closing
optionD: 180 days from the start of sales
explanation: Rule 5110(e)(1) generally bars sale, transfer or hedging of unregistered securities received as underwriting compensation for 180 days beginning on the date of commencement of sales of the public offering.

question: Under FINRA Rule 5121, a member has a conflict of interest in an offering if it will receive at least what share of the net offering proceeds, not counting underwriting compensation?
explanation: Rule 5121(f)(5) defines a conflict of interest to include the member and its affiliates receiving 5 percent or more of the net offering proceeds, as well as control of the issuer, which includes beneficial ownership of 10 percent or more of its common equity.

question: A member that has a conflict of interest in a public offering under Rule 5121 must generally:
optionA: Withdraw from the offering entirely and refund the issuer
optionB: Sell the shares only to institutional investors
optionC: Get each buyer's written consent to the conflict of interest
optionD: Disclose it prominently, usually with a qualified independent underwriter
explanation: Rule 5121 requires prominent disclosure of the conflict and, unless an exception applies (such as a lead manager without a conflict who meets the rule's conditions), participation of a qualified independent underwriter in due diligence.

question: A member sells a private placement covered by FINRA Rule 5123. It must file the offering document with FINRA within:
optionA: 15 calendar days after the first sale
optionB: 3 business days after filing with the SEC
optionC: 30 days before the first sale
optionD: One year after the offering closes
explanation: Rule 5123 requires the member to file the private placement memorandum, term sheet or other offering document with FINRA within 15 calendar days of the date of first sale, or to say none was used.

question: Under FINRA Rule 5122, when a member privately offers its own securities, the offering document must disclose that at least what share of the proceeds will be used for business purposes?
explanation: Rule 5122 requires that at least 85 percent of the offering proceeds be used for business purposes described in the private placement memorandum, which must be filed with FINRA at or before the first time it is given to an investor.

question: Under Rule 506(d) of Regulation D, the exemption is lost if a covered person, such as a paid placement agent, has:
optionA: Sold another private offering earlier that year
optionB: A disqualifying event, such as a recent fraud conviction
optionC: Fewer than 35 accredited investors in the deal
optionD: A customer complaint that was denied
explanation: Rule 506(d), the bad actor rule, disqualifies an offering if the issuer or a covered person, including compensated solicitors and their principals, has a listed disqualifying event, such as certain convictions, orders or bars.

question: An officer of a public company wants to sell shares he bought in the open market years ago. Because he is an affiliate, under Rule 144 his sales are:
optionA: Free of any condition, since he bought them publicly
optionB: Subject to volume limits, with no holding period
optionC: Barred until he leaves the company
optionD: Allowed only through a registered offering
explanation: Shares an affiliate bought in the market are control securities, not restricted securities. They have no holding period, but resales under Rule 144 must meet its volume, manner of sale, current information and notice conditions.

question: Rule 144A provides a safe harbor for resales of restricted securities to:
optionA: Any accredited individual investor
optionB: Retail investors in the issuer's home state
optionC: Employees of the issuer
optionD: Qualified institutional buyers
explanation: Rule 144A lets holders resell restricted securities to qualified institutional buyers, generally institutions that own and invest on a discretionary basis at least $100 million in securities of unaffiliated issuers.

question: Under Regulation M Rule 101, for a security with an ADTV value of at least $100,000 and an issuer public float of at least $25 million, the restricted period begins:
optionA: Five business days before pricing
optionB: One business day before pricing
optionC: The day the registration statement is filed
optionD: Ten business days after the offering closes
explanation: Rule 100 of Regulation M sets a one-business-day restricted period for securities with ADTV of $100,000 or more and a public float of $25 million or more, and five business days for all other securities.

question: Under Regulation M, distribution participants may keep trading an issuer's securities that have an ADTV value of at least $1 million and a public float of at least $150 million because they are:
optionA: Exempt securities
optionB: Restricted control securities
optionC: Actively traded securities
optionD: Penny stocks
explanation: Rule 101 excepts actively-traded securities, defined as those with an ADTV value of at least $1 million issued by an issuer with a public float of at least $150 million, unless the issuer or an affiliate is the distribution participant.

question: Under Regulation M Rule 104, a stabilizing bid in a public offering:
optionA: May be at any price the manager chooses
optionB: May not be above the offering price
optionC: Must be at least 5% above the offering price
optionD: May be made only after the offering closes
explanation: Rule 104 permits stabilizing bids only to prevent or retard a decline, generally at or below the offering price, with notice to the market and disclosure in the prospectus.

question: An investor sold short a stock four business days before a follow-on offering was priced. Under Regulation M Rule 105, the investor:
optionA: Must cover the short through shares in the offering
optionB: Generally may not buy shares in that offering
optionC: May buy shares if they are paid for in cash
optionD: May buy shares but only from another dealer
explanation: Rule 105 bars buying in a firm commitment offering if the person sold short the security during the restricted period, generally the five business days before pricing, subject to limited exceptions.

question: An underwriter defending a Section 11 claim over a misstatement in the registration statement can use the due diligence defense by showing it:
optionA: Investigated reasonably and believed the statements
optionB: Relied only on the issuer's written word
optionC: Was not the lead manager of the deal
optionD: Sold fewer shares than the other underwriters
explanation: Under Section 11(b)(3), an underwriter avoids liability for unexpertised portions if, after reasonable investigation, it had reasonable grounds to believe and did believe the statements were true and complete.

question: Under SEC Rule 14e-1, a tender offer must stay open for at least:
optionA: 20 business days from when it starts
optionB: 5 business days from when it starts
optionC: 30 calendar days from the filing date
optionD: 60 calendar days from the filing date
explanation: Rule 14e-1(a) requires a tender offer to be held open for at least 20 business days, and Rule 14e-1(b) requires at least 10 business days after an increase or decrease in the percentage sought or the consideration offered.

question: During a cash tender offer, Rule 14e-5 generally bars the dealer-manager from:
optionA: Giving holders a copy of the offer document
optionB: Answering holders' questions about the offer
optionC: Being paid a fee by the offeror for its work
optionD: Buying the target's shares outside the offer
explanation: Rule 14e-5 prohibits covered persons, including the offeror and its dealer-manager, from purchasing or arranging to purchase the subject securities except under the tender offer, from announcement until it expires.

question: Since 2024, a person who acquires beneficial ownership of more than 5% of a class of registered equity securities with control intent must file Schedule 13D within:
optionA: Two business days
optionB: Five business days
optionC: Ten calendar days
optionD: 45 days after the calendar year ends
explanation: The SEC's 2023 amendments to Regulation 13D-G, effective February 5, 2024, shortened the initial Schedule 13D filing deadline from 10 calendar days to five business days after crossing 5 percent.

question: A reporting company must generally file a Form 8-K to report a material event, such as entry into a material agreement, within:
optionA: 24 hours of the event
optionB: 15 calendar days of the event
optionC: Four business days of the event
optionD: Its next quarterly report on Form 10-Q
explanation: Form 8-K generally must be filed within four business days after the occurrence of the reportable event.

question: In a corporate liquidation under the absolute priority rule, which class is paid first?
optionA: Preferred stockholders, at liquidation value
optionB: Subordinated debenture holders
optionC: Common stockholders, pro rata
optionD: Secured creditors, from their collateral
explanation: Under the Bankruptcy Code's priority scheme, secured claims are satisfied from their collateral first, then priority and general unsecured claims, subordinated debt, preferred stock and finally common stock.

question: A clause in a loan agreement that bars the borrower from taking on more debt without the lender's consent is:
optionA: A negative covenant
optionB: An affirmative covenant
optionC: A call provision
optionD: A sinking fund provision
explanation: Negative covenants restrict actions such as new borrowing, asset sales or dividends. Affirmative covenants require actions such as delivering financial statements or keeping insurance.

question: A member was an underwriter in a company's IPO. Under Rule 2241 it may not publish research on the company for how long after the IPO date?
optionA: 3 days
optionB: 25 days
optionC: 40 days
optionD: 10 days
explanation: Rule 2241(b)(2)(I)(i) requires a quiet period of at least 10 days after the IPO date for a member that acted as an underwriter or dealer in the IPO.

question: A member acted as co-manager of a secondary offering. Rule 2241 bars it from publishing research on the issuer for how long after the offering date?
optionA: 3 days
optionB: 10 days
optionC: 15 days
optionD: 30 days
explanation: Rule 2241(b)(2)(I)(ii) sets a quiet period of at least three days after a secondary offering for a member that acted as a manager or co-manager.

question: Rule 2241's post-offering quiet periods do not apply when the issuer is:
optionA: An emerging growth company
optionB: Listed on a national exchange
optionC: A foreign private issuer
optionD: A bank holding company
explanation: Rule 2241(b)(2)(I) exempts offerings of emerging growth company securities, consistent with the JOBS Act, from the quiet periods after IPOs and secondary offerings.

question: Under Rule 2241, a research analyst may not:
optionA: Talk with sales staff about a published report
optionB: Attend an industry conference as a speaker
optionC: Help win banking business, such as at pitch meetings
optionD: Meet with company management to check facts
explanation: Rule 2241(b)(2)(L)(i) prohibits research analysts from participating in efforts to solicit investment banking business, including pitches. A limited exception lets analysts attend emerging growth company IPO pitches without soliciting.

question: During a public offering, Rule 2241 bars research analysts from:
optionA: Participating in road shows
optionB: Updating models for other companies
optionC: Reading the issuer's public filings
optionD: Answering investors' questions after the offering
explanation: Rule 2241(b)(2)(L)(ii) prohibits research analysts from participating in road shows and other marketing on behalf of an issuer related to an investment banking services transaction.

question: Before publication, a firm may send the subject company parts of a draft research report to check facts, but only if:
optionA: The company agrees in writing to approve the rating and the target first
optionB: The analyst's supervisor signs and dates each page
optionC: The report has already been sent to customers
optionD: The parts omit the rating and price target, and compliance sees a full draft
explanation: Rule 2241.05 allows sharing sections of a draft for factual review only if they exclude the research summary, rating and price target, and a complete draft is first given to legal or compliance; any later rating change needs written justification and approval.

question: A research report must disclose if the member or its affiliates beneficially own at least what share of a class of the subject company's common equity?
explanation: Rule 2241(c)(4)(F) requires disclosure if the member or its affiliates beneficially own 1 percent or more of any class of common equity of the subject company, measured as of the end of the prior month.

question: A research report must disclose whether the member expects to receive or intends to seek investment banking compensation from the subject company within the next:
optionA: One month
optionB: 12 months
optionC: Two years
optionD: Three months
explanation: Rule 2241(c)(4)(C) requires disclosure of investment banking compensation received in the past 12 months and expected to be received or sought in the next three months.

question: Under Rule 2241, a research analyst's appearance counts as a public appearance when the analyst speaks at a seminar or on a call before at least:
optionA: 5 persons
optionB: 25 persons
optionC: 100 persons
optionD: 15 persons
explanation: Rule 2241(a)(7) defines a public appearance as participation in a conference call, seminar, forum or other public speaking activity before 15 or more persons or before one or more representatives of the media.

question: A firm decides to stop covering a company in its research. Rule 2241 requires it to:
optionA: Get the company's written consent before ending coverage
optionB: Notify customers promptly, with a final report or reason
optionC: Wait one year before ending coverage
optionD: Delete all earlier reports from its website
explanation: Rule 2241(f) requires a member that terminates coverage to notify its customers promptly, using the same means of distribution, with a final report including a final rating or recommendation, or an explanation if one is impractical.

question: Under Rule 2241, a research analyst's pay may NOT be based on:
optionA: The quality and accuracy of research
optionB: Feedback from the firm's customers
optionC: Specific investment banking deals
optionD: Overall productivity of the analyst
explanation: Rule 2241(b)(2) bars compensation based on specific investment banking services transactions or contributions to them, and requires a committee without investment banking representatives to review analyst pay at least annually.

question: Before a firm sends customers research written by an unaffiliated third party that it did not independently select, Rule 2241(h) requires:
optionA: FINRA to review the report before it is sent
optionB: Each customer to agree to receive it
optionC: The third party to register with FINRA
optionD: Approval by a principal or supervisory analyst
explanation: Rule 2241(h)(1) requires a registered principal or supervisory analyst to review and approve third-party research distributed by the member, except independent third-party research that the member does not review or select.

question: Under SEC Regulation AC, a research report must include a certification by the analyst that:
optionA: The firm guarantees the report's price target will be met
optionB: The issuer approved the report's content
optionC: The views reflect the analyst's personal views
optionD: No one at the firm owns the stock
explanation: Regulation AC requires a clear certification that the views accurately reflect the analyst's personal views and a statement whether any part of the analyst's pay was related to the specific recommendations or views.

question: Under FINRA Rule 2242, debt research distributed only to eligible institutional investors:
optionA: Is never allowed under FINRA rules
optionB: Is exempt from many of the rule's requirements
optionC: Must be pre-approved by FINRA before release
optionD: Is exempt from every FINRA rule there is
explanation: Rule 2242 provides an institutional investor exemption: debt research given only to eligible institutional investors is exempt from most of the rule's requirements, though core protections, such as barring retaliation and promises of favorable research, still apply.

question: A firm's compliance department places a company on its confidential watch list because the bankers are working on a deal. The watch list is used to:
optionA: Ban all solicited trades in the stock
optionB: Tell customers that a deal is coming soon
optionC: Monitor trading without public restrictions
optionD: Stop the research department from publishing at all
explanation: A watch list is confidential and lets compliance monitor employee and proprietary trading for misuse of material non-public information. A restricted list, once a deal is public, limits solicitation, trading and research.

question: Rule 2241's exemption from many research separation requirements is available to a member that, over the past three years, averaged no more than 10 managed or co-managed investment banking deals a year and earned no more than:
optionA: $1 million a year in total revenue from all lines
optionB: $50 million a year in total assets
optionC: $5 million a year of investment banking revenue from them
optionD: $25 million a year in commissions from all trading
explanation: Rule 2241(i) exempts members that over the previous three years averaged 10 or fewer investment banking transactions as manager or co-manager a year and generated $5 million or less a year in gross investment banking revenue from them.
